title: Planeswalker's Guide to Nauctis: The Sunken Realm

entities.name: Nauctis
entities.description: A plane of endless ocean, Magic's first underwater plane, where whale gods sing the currents into motion and merfolk civilizations span vast stretches of the sea.

entities.name: Cambra
entities.description: One of the five whale gods of Nauctis, granter of air magic, who surfaces for breath once in a decade; patron of the merfolk.

entities.name: Salinae
entities.description: Whale god of Nauctis who grants tide magic and leads the moon across its path; claimed by merfolk as their creator and patron of the Diluvian League.

entities.name: Lodea
entities.description: Whale god of Nauctis who grants brine magic, whose cadaverous form brings certain death; skeletons animate in her wake.

entities.name: Ruptra
entities.description: Whale god of Nauctis who grants sonic magic and whose song becomes a bellowing cry in times of war.

entities.name: Ethuo
entities.description: Whale god of Nauctis who grants algae magic, whose path erupts with overgrowths of life.

entities.name: Kalekao
entities.description: The dead shark goddess of the chordatans, said to have swum the void between worlds; her teeth litter the ocean floor.

entities.name: Godsongs
entities.description: The ceaseless songs of the whale gods, which grant the ocean its currents and keep Nauctis in balance.

entities.name: Brine magic
entities.description: A swift and toxic death magic granted by Lodea, considered taboo by most merfolk.

entities.name: Deepcalling
entities.description: A Revenist magic of complex rituals allowing them to summon and command colossal monsters of the Abyss.

entities.name: Blood magic
entities.description: Magic wielded by chordatans, extracted from the teeth of their deceased goddess Kalekao.

entities.name: The Abyss
entities.description: The dark, cold, crushing depths beneath the Grand Marine, beneath which an ancient evil seethes.

entities.name: The Grand Marine
entities.description: The deeper, still-lit waters that are the dominion of the merfolk and home to most life on Nauctis.

entities.name: Walking Sea
entities.description: Once the name for the shallowest ocean, now encompassing all the Stranders' territorial claim.

entities.name: Maratheon
entities.description: The capital of the Diluvian League.

entities.name: Halsia
entities.description: An independent merfolk city-state that broke from the Diluvian League under the creed "One mer, one vote."

entities.name: One Tree
entities.description: A sapling in the Strander capital city, the only tree remaining on the plane and the center of Strander faith.

entities.name: Stranders
entities.description: The air-breathers of Nauctis's surface, primarily humans and pinneon, who seek to recreate a fabled world of dry land.

entities.name: Fathom knights
entities.description: An order of human deep-sea divers wearing specialized suits scavenged from the old world.

entities.name: Hyper-Ox
entities.description: The liquid oxygen fathom knights breathe through a lung augment to dive deep for extended periods.

entities.name: Catamarine
entities.description: A pinneon marine fleet and artisan conglomerate of artisans, merchants, mercenaries and guildsfolk.

entities.name: Pinneon
entities.description: Short, fin-footed, whiskered sealfolk who are skilled miners, artificers and sailors.

entities.name: Armada
entities.description: A grand force of cutthroat buccaneers made up almost exclusively of chordatan sharkfolk.

entities.name: Keelhauler armada
entities.description: A famous armada that welcomed fishfolk, homarids, and humans into its ranks.

entities.name: Chordatans
entities.description: Massive, sinuous, amphibious sharkfolk pirates who worship the dead goddess Kalekao.

entities.name: Remora
entities.description: Tiny bipedal fishfolk who happily submit themselves to chordatan crews.

entities.name: Beast sharks
entities.description: Barely sentient, bloodthirsty distant cousins of the chordatans.

entities.name: Merfolk
entities.description: The obligate water-breathing masters of Nauctis's oceans, in the midst of a long golden age.

entities.name: Diluvian Empire
entities.description: The merfolk empire that held its reach for three ages before collapsing in civil conflict.

entities.name: Diluvian League
entities.description: The senatorial merfolk state that rose from the ruins of the Diluvian Empire, the largest faction of its region.

entities.name: Revenist Front
entities.description: A stateless merfolk movement seeking to resurrect the monarchy, secretly following the will of the Abyss and its monsters.

entities.name: Morgriff Reven
entities.description: A magnetic merfolk political dynamo who leads the Revenist Front, believed by followers to be divinely inspired.

entities.name: Noble Serpent
entities.description: A species of colossal monsters able to survive the Abyss, the old symbol of the Diluvian Empire and emblem of the Revenists.

entities.name: Decalids
entities.description: Short-lived squidfolk, remnants of an ancient plane-spanning civilization, who carry ancestor spirits and wield powerful magic.

entities.name: Homarids
entities.description: Functionally immortal crustacean traders and collectors who catalog and preserve the history of Nauctis.

entities.name: Gull aven
entities.description: Avian air-breathers found among the Stranders.

entities.name: Desolators
entities.description: Ravenous elementals born of magma beneath the ocean floor, driven to consume and replace the ocean with slag and pollution.

entities.name: Ruiners
entities.description: Aberrant desolators defined by self-veneration, who organize desolators and attain godlike power.

entities.name: Tecton
entities.description: The first ruiner, a desolator whose directive deformed into the single thought to become god.

entities.name: Wandering Era
entities.description: The legendary first era of merfolk history, populated by heroes and savants.

entities.name: Years of Crying Bells
entities.description: The cataclysmic civil conflict that ended the Diluvian Empire, fought between traditionalists and revolutionaries.

events.summary: In the plane's distant past, the five whale gods emerged from leylines near the dawn of Nauctis.
events.quote: These colossal beings are spun from raw mana, having emerged from leylines near the dawn of the plane.

events.summary: In ancient history, the decalid empire rose and then collapsed under its own weight.
events.quote: Their might surged alongside that of the ocean—an avaricious expansion that swiftly fell apart under its own weight.

events.summary: After the Wandering Era, merfolk settlements clashed and grew into kingdoms, from which the Diluvian Empire rose.
Civil conflict between traditionalists and revolutionaries broke out in the Diluvian Empire during the Years of Crying Bells.
events.quote: Civil conflict flared in a period now known as the Years of Crying Bells.

events.summary: Both sides beseeched Ruptra, who rejected them and raged across their battlefields until she forced a ceasefire.
events.quote: eventually forced a ceasefire by virtue of leaving nothing behind to fight over.

events.summary: The Diluvian League rose from the Empire's ruins, governed by a senate instead of a monarch.
events.quote: The Diluvian League rose from the ruins of the Empire, now led by a senate rather than a monarch.

events.summary: Halsia split from the League's control and declared independence.
events.quote: The city-state Halsia split from their control at the same time and declared its independence.

events.summary: Monarchist traditionalists gathered as the Revenists, awaiting the Empire's return.
events.quote: traditionalists of the old monarchical power gathered under the name "Revenist," biding their time for the Empire's return.

events.summary: Halsia defended its independence against the League, leading to the present tense ceasefire.
events.quote: Ultimately, Halsia protected its independence, leading to the tense ceasefire of the present day.

events.summary: Having consumed all biomass in their region of the Abyss, the desolators rose higher and clashed violently with the Grand Marine's inhabitants.
events.quote: This has caused violent clashing with the inhabitants of the Grand Marine, earning them their name, "desolators."

events.summary: An aberrant desolator achieved apotheosis and became Tecton, the first ruiner, allowing more ruiners to follow.
events.quote: It was apotheosis. The first ruiner was born: Tecton

relations.note: Merfolk claim Salinae as their creator.
relations.quote: They claim the god Salinae as their creator and Cambra as their patron.

relations.note: Cambra is the merfolk's patron god.
relations.quote: They claim the god Salinae as their creator and Cambra as their patron.

relations.note: Salinae is the League's patron god.
relations.quote: The League's patron god is Salinae, mother of oceans.

relations.note: The Front is named after him and he spearheaded it.
relations.quote: the Revenist Front, named after the magnetic dynamo who spearheaded their mobilization.

relations.note: They follow the will of the Abyss and its monsters.
relations.quote: They follow the will of the Abyss and the monsters therein.

relations.note: The Noble Serpent embodies their movement.
relations.quote: His movement is embodied by the old symbol of the Diluvian Empire: the Noble Serpent

relations.note: They fought the Years of Crying Bells and now hold a tense ceasefire.
relations.quote: This clash of wills led to bloody conflict, now known as the Years of Crying Bells.

relations.note: Halsian druids connect deeply with Ethuo.
relations.quote: Druids connect deeply with Ethuo and his domain, allowing them to commune with nature.

relations.note: Successor state of the Empire.
relations.quote: The Diluvian League rose from the ruins of the Empire, now led by a senate rather than a monarch.

relations.note: Capital of the League.
relations.quote: Dozens of provinces encompass Diluvia's capital Maratheon

relations.note: The pinneon of the Catamarine are among the Stranders.
relations.quote: They are among the ranks of the Stranders, toiling alongside humanity across the plane's meager surface.

relations.note: The Catamarine is made up of pinneon sealfolk.
relations.quote: These proud and daring sealfolk make up the Catamarine

relations.note: Stranders live most populously in the Walking Sea.
relations.quote: They live most populously in the Walking Sea

relations.note: Chordatans worship the dead goddess Kalekao.
relations.quote: The chordatans worship a dead god: Kalekao, the shark who was said to swim the void between worlds.

relations.note: Remora submit to chordatan crews.
relations.quote: tiny bipedal fishfolk who happily submit themselves to chordatan crews.

relations.note: Distant cousins.
relations.quote: They share distant cousinhood with the behemoth beast sharks

relations.note: The Armada raids Stranders and merfolk alike.
relations.quote: They raid both the surface and the Grand Marine, a plague on Stranders and merfolk alike.

relations.note: Decalids hold particular loyalty to Lodea.
relations.quote: Their short lifespans ensure they have a particular loyalty to Lodea

relations.note: Homarids fear and respect Lodea.
relations.quote: they fear Lodea, but they also respect her, draw strength from her

relations.note: The Abyss lies below the Grand Marine.
relations.quote: Skulking below the Grand Marine is the Abyss.

relations.note: Tecton was the first ruiner.
relations.quote: The first ruiner was born: Tecton

relations.note: Ruiners compel desolators to organize and command their reverence.
relations.quote: Their presence compels all desolators around them to organize and mobilize in ways they never could before.

relations.note: Desolators clash violently with inhabitants of the Grand Marine.
relations.quote: This has caused violent clashing with the inhabitants of the Grand Marine
